findings.title: Migrate or version Redis keys before changing sets to sorted sets
findings.body: The new ZADD and ZSCAN operations reuse the same span-buf:s:* keys that the previous consumer populated with Redis sets. Existing buffered segments therefore cause WRONGTYPE errors on insertion or flushing after deployment; during a rolling deployment, old and new consumers also cannot read each other's buffers. This can stall ingestion and leave buffered spans to expire without being produced. Use a versioned namespace with a drain strategy, or explicitly migrate existing keys before switching operations.

findings.title: Use datetime cursor conversion for the audit-log paginator
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint selects this paginator with order_by='-datetime', but get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on AuditLogEntry.datetime, which is a datetime object rather than a number. An optimized request with any results therefore raises TypeError while building its cursors instead of returning audit logs. value_from_cursor also returns the numeric cursor unchanged rather than converting it to a datetime for the database comparison. Inherit DateTimePaginator or implement its timestamp conversions.

findings.title: Reject negative offsets instead of passing them to Django slicing
findings.body: The advanced path passes a negative cursor.offset directly to a Django QuerySet slice. Django explicitly rejects negative indexing with ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'); it does not handle the boundary automatically as the comment claims. Consequently, the advertised negative-offset feature fails for an authorized optimized request such as cursor=0:-1:0. Validate and reject such cursors as invalid pagination, or translate them into supported nonnegative query bounds.

findings.title: Honor the configured span-count limit during eviction
findings.body: Eviction is hard-coded to 1000 spans while SpansBuffer still accepts and stores max_segment_spans, and the flush-time enforcement of that parameter has been removed. A caller configuring a smaller limit now receives segments above that limit, while a caller configuring a larger limit silently loses spans at 1000. Pass the configured limit to the script and apply it there, or explicitly remove the configuration contract rather than leaving it ineffective.
